A manifesto issued by the Kuomintang
Party on the subject of
its re-organization.

This Party was first known as the Revolutionary
Party. Later it became known as Kuomintang Party.
From a secret organization this Party became a public
political party. It has a history of about 20 years
and has been engaged in many struggles: the battle at
Canton in March of 1911 and the battle at Hankow in
October of the same year were the principal ones. This
Party did its work in the overthrow of Yuan Shih Kai
in the year 1915 and in the preservation of the
Constitution in the year 1916. Countless members
of the Party sacrificed their lives for an individual
or for the Party. He who resisted the Party was
put down and he who opposed the Party was annihilated.
The determination of the members and their sacrifices
have been unsurpassed by any other Party in the country,
but considering the work during the past ten years
we must confess that the Party has been a failure.
After the overthrow of the Ching Dynasty Yuan Shih Kai
was made President and after the suppression of the
Hung Hsien Movement the country was divided into small
republic states of tyranny, whilst the militarists
clung to it recklessly and politicians did a lot of
harm to the country. Many members of the Party sided
with the wicked and a number of M.P.s sold themselves.
The condition of the country appeared to be like a
prairie on fire or to the drifted waters of the Huang
Ho (Yellow River). The people had been led to believe
that a revolution would not set the country on a firmer
standing and they would not be able to undertake
anything. This is exactly the situation of the
country today.

China has been badly administered. Finances are
low and the country has been divided into sections and
is face to face with crisis. If we want to save China
from extermination, the formation of a properly
disciplined and organized political Party is absolutely
necessary. This Party will carry out the wishes of
the people and direct them to fight for the right cause,
thereby attaining their objects, otherwise the people
will not know what to do and are sure to be treated by
the militarists as "Cows and horses", and fall victims
to foreign capitalism and imperialism. It is disgraceful
to talk of the political parties in China. They are with
one party in the morning and in the evening they have
become attached to another party. In short, they have
no fixed objects. They care for their personal interests
only and do not care even if they be slaves. There are
numerous such parties in the country. But for many years
this Party has been fighting for the freedom of the people,
for their rights and their lives. Although during these
years the name of the Party had undergone several changes
yet it has always stood by its objects.

The reason why this Party has failed to accomplish
anything is because it had not been properly organized
and disciplined. It is known to every one that no matter
how big an army may be it will not win a victory unless
it is properly disciplined. This Party has realized its
defects and has therefore decided on re-organization. The
leader of the Party will appoint a Central Executive Committee
of 9 persons to start the re-organization and a conference

国民党关于其改组事宜发布的宣言。

本党初名为革命党。后更名为国民党。本党由秘密组织转变为公开政党。迄今约有二十年历史，历经多次斗争：其中主要者为1911年3月的广州战役及同年10月的汉口战役。本党在1915年致力于推翻袁世凯，并在1916年致力于维护宪法。无数党员为个人或为本党牺牲生命。抗拒本党者被镇压，反对本党者被消灭。党员之决心与牺牲精神，国内无其他政党能出其右，但回顾过去十年之工作，我们必须承认本党是失败的。清朝覆灭后，袁世凯就任总统，洪宪运动被镇压后，国家分裂为若干施行暴政的小共和国，军阀肆意把持政权，政客对国家造成极大危害。许多党员与奸恶之徒同流合污，部分议员出卖自身。国家局势犹如草原烈火，又似黄河漂流的洪水。民众已被引导相信革命无法使国家根基稳固，因而无力承担任何事业。这正是当今国家的状况。

中国治理不善。财政匮乏，国家四分五裂，面临危机。若欲挽救中国免于灭亡，组建一个纪律严明、组织得当的政党绝对必要。本党将贯彻民众意愿，引导他们为正义事业而奋斗，从而实现其目标；否则，民众将不知所措，必被军阀视如“牛马”，并沦为外国资本主义和帝国主义的牺牲品。谈及中国的政党令人蒙羞。他们早晨依附一党，晚上便转投另一党。简言之，他们没有固定目标。他们只关心个人利益，即便沦为奴隶也在所不惜。国内此类政党众多。但多年来，本党一直为人民的自由、权利和生命而战。尽管这些年本党名称几经变更，但始终坚守其目标。

本党未能成就任何事业的原因，在于其组织和纪律不当。众所周知，无论军队规模多大，若纪律不严，便无法取胜。本党已认识到自身缺陷，因此决定进行改组。党领袖将任命一个由9人组成的中央执行委员会以启动改组工作，随后将召开来自全国及海外各分支的代表会议讨论此事。

Mingkuopao
Regtd. Jap. Cons.
1-1-24

Draft Regulations of the Kuomintang
Party in China.

Chapter 1 ---- Membership.

Art. 1. Anyone who observes the regulations --
of the Party, attend a branch office of this
Party, carry out its resolutions and pay the
membership fee in due time is allowed to be
a member of the Party.
Art. 2. Anyone who wishes to join the Party must
be introduced by more than two members of the
Party.
Art. 3. The admission of any person to membership
of the Party at any place must first be passed
by a general meeting of the members of the
Party of the place concerned.
Art. 4. In case a member removes from one place
to another, he must report himself at the
branch of the place to which he has removed
and will henceforth be attached to that
branch.

Chapter 2 ----- The Organization
of the Party.

Art. 5. The branch which deals with matters of
the Party in a whole district is regarded as
the superior establishment and that which
deals with matters of only a section of the
Party is regarded as a subordinate establishment.
Art. 6. All matters concerning a district may be
dealt with by the district branch Party.
Art. 7. The branch parties at various places
should regard the National Delegates Congress,
the District Delegates Congress and the
district Members Congress as superior
establishments.
Art. 8. The National Delegates Congress, the
District Delegates Congress and the District
Members Congress should each elect an
Executive Committee for the discharge of their
respective duties.
Art. 9. The Party is divided into the following
sections:-
(A) National--
National Delegates Congress--
Central Executive Committee.
(B) Provincial--
Provincial Delegates Congress--
Provincial Executive Committee.
(C) Prefectural--
Prefectural Delegates Congress--
Prefectural Executive Committee.
(D) District--
District Delegates Congress--
District Executive Committee.
(E) Sub-District--
Sub-District Members Congress--
Sub-District Executive Committee, the
Sub-District Members Congress being the
original form of organization.
Art. 10. The Executive Sections of the Party are
as follows:
(A) The National Delegates Congress--
When not in session this body functions as
the Central Executive Committee.
(B) The Provincial Delegates Congress--
When not in session this body functions as
the Provincial Executive Committee.

民国日报
日本领事馆注册
1924年1月1日

中国国民党章程草案。

第一章 ---- 党员。

第一条. 凡遵守本党章程、参加本党分部、执行本党决议并按时缴纳党费者，准予成为本党党员。
第二条. 凡欲入党者，须由两名以上本党党员介绍。
第三条. 任何地方的人员加入本党，须先经该地党员大会通过。
第四条. 若党员从一地迁往另一地，须向迁入地的分部报到，此后即隶属于该分部。

第二章 ----- 党的组织。

第五条. 负责处理整个区域党务的分部视为上级机构，仅负责处理局部党务的分部视为下级机构。
第六条. 涉及整个区域的所有事务可由区党部处理。
第七条. 各地分部应将全国代表大会、区代表大会及区党员大会视为上级机构。
第八条. 全国代表大会、区代表大会及区党员大会应分别选举执行委员会，以履行各自职责。
第九条. 本党分为以下各部：-
(A) 全国级--
全国代表大会--
中央执行委员会。
(B) 省级--
省代表大会--
省执行委员会。
(C) 府级--
府代表大会--
府执行委员会。
(D) 区级--
区代表大会--
区执行委员会。
(E) 分区级--
分区党员大会--
分区执行委员会，分区党员大会为组织的原始形式。
第十条. 本党的执行部门如下：
(A) 全国代表大会--
休会期间，由中央执行委员会行使职权。
(B) 省代表大会--
休会期间，由省执行委员会行使职权。

pages.en:
(U) The Prefectural Delegates Congress--
When not in session this body functions as
the Prefectural Executive Committee.
(D) District Delegates Congress--
When not in session this body functions as
the District Executive Committee.
(E) Sub-District Members Congress--
When not in session this body functions as
the Sub-District Executive Committee.
All Executive Sections should carry out
the orders and resolutions of the superior
Sections, but they may protest against
any resolutions passed by the latter.
Art. 11. The Central Executive Committee and the
Provincial Executive Committee may establish
various departments for the discharge of the
duties of the Party- ordinary or extraordinary.
All these departments will be under the control
of their respective Executive Committees. The
duties of the departments and the method of
their organization must be decided upon by the
Central Executive Committee.
Art. 12. The Executive Committees of the minor sections
are under the control of the Provincial Executive
Committee, which, in turn, is under the orders
of the Central Executive Committee.
Art. 13. The seals of the Executive Committees of the
various Sections are not to be taken into use
unless permission is first obtained from the
superior Sections.
Art. 14. Every member of the Party should get a
membership certificate from the branch with
which he is connected. The contents and the
form of the certificate are to be decided upon
by the Central Executive Committee.

Chapter 3----The Highest Section
of the Party.

Art. 15. The highest section of the Party is the National
Delegates congress which meets once a year. When
the Central Executive Committee deems it necessary
or when it is requested by one-third of the
members of the last National Delegates conference,
a special national delegates conference may be
called at any time.
Art. 16. The date of the National Delegates Conference
must be made known to all members of the Party
at least two months beforehand and the date of
the special national delegates conference at least
three months in advance.
Art. 17. The National Delegates Conference is in session
when attendance reaches one-half of that of the
last conference.
Art. 18. The organization of the National Delegates
Conference and the number of delegates to be sent
by each place are to be fixed by the Central
Executive Committee.
Art. 19. The duties of the National Delegates Conference
are as follows:
(A) To accept and adopt at its discretion
the reports of the Central Executive Committee
and other central departments.
(B) To revise the regulations of the
Party.
(C) To decide what policy to be adopted
towards events of the day.
pages.zh:
(U) 府代表大会--
休会期间，由府执行委员会行使职权。
(D) 区代表大会--
休会期间，由区执行委员会行使职权。
(E) 分区党员大会--
休会期间，由分区执行委员会行使职权。
所有执行部门应执行上级部门的命令和决议，但可对后者通过的决议提出抗议。
第十一条. 中央执行委员会和省执行委员会可设立各种部门，以履行本党常规或非常规职责。所有这些部门均受各自执行委员会管辖。各部门的职责及其组织方法须由中央执行委员会决定。
第十二条. 较小部门的执行委员会受省执行委员会管辖，而省执行委员会则受中央执行委员会指挥。
第十三条. 各部门执行委员会的印章，须先获得上级部门许可方可启用。
第十四条. 每位党员应从其所属分部获取党员证。证书的内容和格式由中央执行委员会决定。

第三章----党的最高部门。

第十五条. 党的最高部门为全国代表大会，每年召开一次。当中央执行委员会认为有必要，或经上一届全国代表大会三分之一代表请求时，可随时召开特别全国代表大会。
第十六条. 全国代表大会的日期须至少提前两个月通知全体党员，特别全国代表大会的日期须至少提前三个月通知。
第十七条. 当出席人数达到上一届大会的一半时，全国代表大会即构成法定会议。
第十八条. 全国代表大会的组织及各地方派遣的代表人数由中央执行委员会确定。
第十九条. 全国代表大会的职责如下：
(A) 酌情接受并通过中央执行委员会及其他中央部门的报告。
(B) 修订党章。
(C) 决定对时局事件采取的政策。

pages.en:
(D) To elect the leader of the
Party, the members of the Central Executive
Committee, the reserve members of this
Committee and the investigation Committee
Art. 20. The number of members of the Central Executive
Committee and the Investigation Committee are
to be fixed by the National Delegates Congress.
Art. 21. Upon a member of the Central Executive Committee
retiring, the vacancy is to be filled by a
reserve member of the Committee in consecutive
order.
Art. 22. The duties of the Central Executive Committee
are as follows:
(A) To represent the Party in
Diplomatic affairs.
(B) To organize branches in various
places and to direct them.
(C) To appoint the staff of the
newspaper of the Party.
(D) To organize the various
departments of the Central Section of the Party.
(E) To take charge of the finances
of the Party.
Art. 23. Members of the Party in Government services or
in the service of clubs, social organizations,
labour organizations, commercial organizations,
District Assemblies, Prefectural Assemblies,
Provincial Assemblies and Parliament should
organize member groups. The Central Executive
Committee should direct them to do so.
Art. 24. The Central Executive Committee should hold
a meeting at least every two weeks in which the
reserve members of the committee may participate
but they may express opinions only.
Art. 25. The leader of the Party should occupy the
chair at the meetings of the Central Executive
Committee.
Art. 26. The Central Executive Committee should elect
three secretaries, establish a secretariat to
carry out daily routine work.
Art. 27. When the National Delegates Conference is not
in session the Central Executive Committee should
call a meeting of the Provincial Executive
committees and the delegates of the branch
Parties in various places.
Art. 28. The Central Executive Committee should send once
a month an account of its activities to the
Provincial Executive Committees and Provincial
board of managers.

Chapter 4---- Investigation Committee.

Art. 29. The National Delegates Conference should elect
three members as the Executive Investigation
Committee; the duties of which are to be as
follows:
(A) To take charge of the finances of
the Central Executive Committee.
(B) To investigate into the condition
of the Party and the personal conduct of the
members. The Executive Investigation Committee
is empowered to give orders to the lower
departments of the Party in matters of finance
and other matters closely affecting the Party.

Chapter 5---- Provincial Branch Parties.

Art. 30. The Provincial Delegates Congress should hold a
session every six months, but if ordered by the

第二十条. 中央执行委员会和调查委员会的成员人数由全国代表大会确定。
第二十一条. 中央执行委员会委员出缺时，由候补委员按顺序递补。
第二十二条. 中央执行委员会的职责如下：
(A) 在外交事务中代表本党。
(B) 在各地组织分部并对其进行指导。
(C) 任命本党报社工作人员。
(D) 组织本党中央部的各个部门。
(E) 掌管本党财务。
第二十三条. 在政府服务或在俱乐部、社会组织、劳工组织、商业组织、区议会、府议会、省议会及国会服务的党员，应组织党员小组。中央执行委员会应指导其这样做。
第二十四条. 中央执行委员会应至少每两周举行一次会议，委员会候补委员可参加，但仅可发表意见。
第二十五条. 党领袖应在中央执行委员会会议上担任主席。
第二十六条. 中央执行委员会应选举三名秘书，设立秘书处以处理日常例行工作。
第二十七条. 全国代表大会休会期间，中央执行委员会应召集省执行委员会及各地分部代表开会。
第二十八条. 中央执行委员会应每月向省执行委员会及省管理部发送一次活动报告。

第四章---- 调查委员会。

第二十九条. 全国代表大会应选举三名成员组成执行调查委员会；其职责如下：
(A) 掌管中央执行委员会的财务。
(B) 调查党的状况及党员的个人行为。执行调查委员会有权在财务及其他密切影响党的事务上向党下级部门下达命令。

第五章---- 省级分部。

第三十条. 省代表大会应每六个月召开一次会议，但若奉

pages.en:
Central Executive Committee or requested by the
Prefectural Executive Committee and District
Executive Committee, a meeting may be called at
any time.
Art. 31. If the Provincial Executive committee deems
it necessary or if requested by one-half of
the members of the Provincial Branch Party,
a special provincial delegates meeting may
be convened.
Art. 32. The method of electing delegates to attend
the Provincial Delegates Conference and the
number of delegates are to be fixed by the
Provincial Executive Committee with the
approval of the various Prefectural Executive
Committees.
Art. 33. The Provincial Delegates Conference should
accept and adopt at its discretion the reports
of the Provincial Executive Committee and of
other provincial departments of the Party.
It should also elect members of the Provincial
Executive Committee and of the Investigation
Committee.
Art. 34. The duties of the Provincial Executive
Committees are as follows:-
(A) To establish a secretariat of
three persons.
(B) To establish provincial branch
parties and to direct same.
(C) To appoint a staff for the
newspaper of the Party in a province.
(D) To establish various departments
of the Party in each province.
(E) To take charge of the finances
of the Party.
Art. 35. The Provincial Executive Committee should
forward an account of its activities to the
Central Executive Committee once a month.
Art. 36. The Provincial Executive Committee should
hold a meeting every two weeks. The reserve
members of the Committee may attend the
meeting at which they may only express their
opinions.
Art. 37. If a member of the Provincial Executive
Committee retires, the vacancy is to be filled
by a reserve member of the Committee in
consecutive order.
Art. 38. The Provincial Investigation Committee may
regulate the finances of the Provincial
Executive Committee and investigate its work
or inquire into the conduct of the members
of the provincial branch parties.

Chapter 6---- Prefectural Branch
Parties

Art. 39. The Prefectural Delegates Congress should hold
a meeting every three months. A special
prefectural delegates conference may be called
at any time on the orders of the Provincial
Executive Committee or at the request of the
various district Executive Committees.
Art. 40. When the Prefectural Executive Committee
deems it necessary or at the request of half of
the members of the Prefectural branch party,
a special prefectural delegates meeting may be
called.
pages.zh:
中央执行委员会或应府级执行委员会及区级执行委员会之请求，可随时召开会议。

第三十一条。若省执行委员会认为有必要，或经省分部党员半数之请求，可召开特别省代表会议。

第三十二条。出席省代表会议之代表选举方法及代表人数，由省执行委员会拟定，并经各府级执行委员会批准后确定。

第三十三条。省代表会议应酌情接受并通过省执行委员会及党在省其他各部门之报告。会议亦应选举省执行委员会委员及调查委员会委员。

第三十四条。省执行委员会之职责如下：
（甲）设立由三人组成之秘书处。
（乙）建立省分部并予以指导。
（丙）委任省内党报之工作人员。
（丁）在各省设立党之各部。
（戊）掌管党之财务。

第三十五条。省执行委员会应每月向中央执行委员会呈报一次活动情况。

第三十六条。省执行委员会应每两周举行一次会议。委员会候补委员可列席会议，但仅有权发表意见。

第三十七条。若省执行委员会委员离职，其空缺应由委员会候补委员按顺序递补。

第三十八条。省调查委员会可监管省执行委员会之财务，调查其工作，或查究省分部党员之行为。

第六章----府级分部

第三十九条。府级代表大会应每三个月举行一次会议。根据省执行委员会之命令或应各區执行委员会之请求，可随时召开特别府级代表会议。

第四十条。当府级执行委员会认为有必要，或经府级分部党员半数之请求，可召开特别府级代表会议。

pages.en:
Art. 41. The procedure to be adopted in the election
of delegates to attend the Prefectural Delegates
meeting and the number of such delegates are
to be fixed by the Prefectural Executive Committee.
Art. 42. The Prefectural Delegates Congress may accept
and adopt the reports of the Prefectural
Executive Committee and of other departments
of the Party in the prefecture; it should also
elect members of the Prefectural Executive
Committee, the reserve members of this Committee
and the members of the Investigation Committee.
Art. 43. The Prefectural Executive Committee may
elect a secretary to carry out routine affairs,
establish prefectural branch parties and
directs same, appoint with the approval of
the Provincial Executive Committee the staff
of the paper, which is the organ of the Party
in the prefecture, organize the various
departments of the Party and regulate the
finance and expenditure of the branch parties
in the prefecture.
Art. 44. The Prefectural Executive Committee should
forward an account of its activities every
two weeks to the Provincial Executive Committee.
Art. 45. The Prefectural Executive Committee must
meet once a week. The reserve members of
the committee may attend but they will have
only the right of expressing their opinions.
Art.46. If a member of the Prefectural Executive
Committee retires, a reserve member of the
committee may fill the vacancy by rotation.

Chapter 7----District Branch Parties.

Art. 47. The highest body in a district is the
District Members Association or the District
Delegates Association. A district members
association comprises the members of the branches
in villages and towns. In case the villages
or towns are too far away from the district or
the number of members is too large, instead of
holding a members meeting a conference of delegates
should be held, and this body is to be regarded
as the highest in the district, but whenever
possible meetings of members should be held.
Art. 48. Meetings of members and of delegates should
be held once a month when matters of the following
nature are to be discussed:-
(A) Admittance to membership.
(B) Acceptance and adoption of the
report of the District Executive Committee.
(C) The delegates participating in the
Delegates conference and the members
participating in the meeting of members
should report to the association the condition
of the branch parties, solve the difficult
problems confronting the branch parties, and give
their views of political and financial matters.
(D) To persuade members to observe the
regulations of the Party, to solve the
problem of illiteracy, to raise money to
defray the expenses of the Party and to
discuss the resolutions, if any, passed by
the Prefectural Executive Committee and the
pages.zh:
第四十一条。出席府级代表会议之代表选举程序及代表人数，由府级执行委员会确定。

第四十二条。府级代表大会可接受并通过府级执行委员会及党内府级其他各部门之报告；会议亦应选举府级执行委员会委员、该委员会候补委员及调查委员会委员。

第四十三条。府级执行委员会可选举一名秘书处理日常事务，建立府级分部并予以指导，经省执行委员会批准后委任作为党在府级机关报之工作人员，组织党之各部，并规范府内各分部之财务及支出。

第四十四条。府级执行委员会应每两周向省执行委员会呈报一次活动情况。

第四十五条。府级执行委员会必须每周开会一次。委员会候补委员可列席，但仅享有发表意见之权。

第四十六条。若府级执行委员会委员离职，可由委员会候补委员轮流递补空缺。

第七章----区分部

第四十七条。区内最高机构为区党员大会或区代表会。区党员大会由村镇各分部之党员组成。若村镇距离区署过远或党员人数过多，则不应举行党员大会，而应举行代表会议，该机构被视为区内最高机构，但在可能情况下仍应举行党员大会。

第四十八条。党员大会及代表会议应每月举行一次，讨论下列事项：
（甲）接纳新党员。
（乙）接受并通过区执行委员会之报告。
（丙）参加代表会议之代表及参加党员大会之党员，应向协会报告分部状况，解决分部面临之困难问题，并就政治及财政事项发表意见。
（丁）劝诫党员遵守党规，解决文盲问题，筹集资金以支付党务费用，并讨论府级执行委员会及

pages.en:
District Executive Committee.
(E) To elect the Executive
Committee of their respective districts.
Art. 49. The District Executive Committee directs the
sub-District parties and other organs in the
district, takes charge of the registration of
members, convenes the citizens' Conference,
organizes the sub-district branch parties, and
with the approval of the Prefectural Executive
Committee, which must first be obtained, regulates
the expenditure and finance of the Party. The
District Executive Committee must forward to the
Prefectural Executive Committee a detailed
account of its activities every two weeks.

Chapter 8---- Sub-District
Members Association.

Art. 50. The sub-district members Association is the most
subordinate organization of the Party. It is
organized by the District Executive Committee
or other district bodies functioning as the
District Executive Committee or it may be organized
by the members themselves with the approval of
the Prefectural Executive Committee. The number
of members of a sub-district Association is unlimited,
but can not be fewer than 5.
Art. 51. The sub-district association is formed for the
purpose of communicating with the members of
district association; and in places where there
are only sub-district associations, they are to
be regarded as the highest establishment, and their
duties are as follows:-
(A) To carry out the decisions of the
Party.
(B) To secure members.
(C) To assist the District Executive
Committee in the routine work of the Party.
(D) To propagate the objects of the Party.
(E) To collect membership fees, to look
after the sale of stamps of the Party,
commemoration cards and badges.
(F) To elect delegates to attend the
general conference, the Prefectural Conference,
the Provincial Conference, and the National
Conference.
(G) To carry out the orders of the highest
organization.
Art. 52. The sub-district Association should elect three
men as a sub-district Executive Committee to carry
out its routine work. The Sub-District Executive
Committee should have one secretary who is to forward
every two weeks to the District Executive Committee
an account of the activities of the Party.

Chapter 9---- Discipline.

Art. 53. All members of the Party must observe the
regulations of the Party, abide by the objects of
the Party and accept service with the Party in time
of military operations. All matters connected with
the Party may be freely discussed, but when
resolutions have been passed all must act in harmony.
(Note) This Party is to fight for the future
good of the country. The preservation of our colonies,
freedom and the peace of the people will all depend
pages.zh:
区执行委员会通过之决议（如有）。
（戊）选举各自辖区之执行委员会。

第四十九条。区执行委员会指导区内子区分部及其他机构，负责党员登记，召集市民会议，组织子区分部，并在事先获得府级执行委员会批准之情况下，规范党之支出及财务。区执行委员会必须每两周向府级执行委员会呈报详细之活动账目。

第八章----子区党员协会

第五十条。子区党员协会是党之最基层组织机构。它由区执行委员会或其他行使区执行委员会职能之区级机构组建，或在获得府级执行委员会批准后由党员自行组建。子区协会会员人数不限，但不得少于五人。

第五十一条。组建子区协会旨在与区协会会员进行沟通；在仅有子区协会之地，它们被视为最高建制，其职责如下：
（甲）执行党之决定。
（乙）招募党员。
（丙）协助区执行委员会处理党之日常事务。
（丁）宣传党之宗旨。
（戊）收取党费，负责党之邮票、纪念卡及徽章之销售事宜。
（己）选举代表出席总会议、府级会议、省级会议及全国会议。
（庚）执行最高组织之命令。

第五十二条。子区协会应选举三人组成子区执行委员会，以处理日常事务。子区执行委员会应设秘书一名，每两周向区执行委员会呈报党务活动情况。

第九章----纪律

第五十三条。所有党员必须遵守党规，恪守党之宗旨，并在军事行动期间接受党之服役安排。所有与党有关之事项均可自由讨论，但一旦决议通过，所有人必须一致行动。
（注）本党为国家未来之福祉而战。我们殖民地之保全、自由及人民之和平均将依赖

pages.en:
on the success of the Party. In order to attain
our objects discipline will be strictly enforced.
The success or failure of the Party will depend
ultimately on this. All are expected to take note.
Art. 54. Any member of the Party who fails to observe
the resolutions of the Party, commits an infringement
of the regulations, thereby violating the objects
of the Party. He is liable the following grades
of punishment: To be reprimanded either publicly or
in the presence of the members, and the details
of the affair are to be published in the papers of
the Party; he will be suspended temporarily or
permanently. Any member who has been dismissed
from the Party will no longer be allowed to enter
Government service or other establishments which
are under the control of this Party. If all the
members of a branch party in a certain place fail
to observe the regulations of the Party, thereby
violating its objects etc., the whole branch will
be dissolved, a report will be published in the
paper of the Party and all the members will be
dismissed.
Art. 55. Upon a member or a branch party being suspended
the Investigation Committee of the branch should
make exhaustive enquiries and the Executive Committee
of the branch should give decision. If the Executive
Committee finds the suspension unjustified an appeal
may be made to the higher Executive Committee or
to the National Congress, but the member will remain
in suspension until the decision has been given
by the National Congress. The National Congress
may restore a member or a branch party, but the
decision is ineffective until it is approved of by
the Central Executive Committee.

Chapter 10---- Expenditure.

Art. 56. The expenditure of the Party is covered by the
membership fees and other incomes or with the
contributions from headquarters.
Art. 57. Each member is to pay 20 cents per month as
membership fee. A member who is out of employment
or ill may be exempted from payment when a record
of this effect will be made by the branch Party
with which he is connected. A report to this
effect must be made by the Party concerned to the
highest Executive Committee.
Art. 58. Any member who fails to pay his fee for a period
of 3 months without permission, will be deprived
of membership.

Chapter 11---- Kuomintang Groups.

Art. 59. Members of the Party who are serving or connected
with any labour organizations, clubs, social
organizations, commercial organizations, educational
organizations , Town Assemblies, Prefectural
Assemblies, Provincial Assemblies or Parliament
should form Kuomintang groups in order to induce
those who are not members of the Party to join,
thereby extending the influence of the Party and
its activities.
Art. 60. The movements of members who are connected with
non-Kuomintang organizations will be controlled by the
Central Executive Committee.

第五十四条。任何党员若不遵守党之决议，违反规章，从而违背党之宗旨，将受以下等级之处分：予以公开或在党员面前之申斥，并将事件详情刊登于党报；予以暂时或永久停职。任何被开除出党之成员，将不再被允许进入政府服务部门或受本党控制之其他机构任职。若某地一分部之全体党员未能遵守党规，从而违背其宗旨等，则该分部将被解散，相关报告将刊登于党报，且所有党员将被开除。

第五十五条。当党员或分部被停职时，该分部之调查委员会应进行详尽调查，并由该分部之执行委员会作出裁决。若执行委员会认定停职不当，可向上一级执行委员会或全国代表大会提出上诉，但在全国代表大会作出裁决之前，该党员仍保持停职状态。全国代表大会可恢复党员或分部之资格，但该决定在未经中央执行委员会批准前无效。

第十章----支出

第五十六条。党之支出由党费及其他收入或总部之拨款承担。

第五十七条。每名党员每月需缴纳二十仙作为党费。失业或患病之党员可免缴，但其所属分部须对此情况进行记录。相关党派必须就此情况向最高执行委员会呈报。

第五十八条。任何党员若未经许可连续三个月未缴纳党费，将被剥夺党员资格。

第十一章----国民党小组

第五十九条。在任何劳工组织、俱乐部、社会组织、商业组织、教育组织、市议会、府议会、省议会或国会中任职或与上述机构有关联之党员，应组建国民党小组，以诱导非党员加入，从而扩大党之影响力及其活动范围。

第六十条。与非国民党组织有关联之党员之行动，将由中央执行委员会控制。

Art. 61. The Kuomintang groups should place themselves
under the orders of the Executive Committee of
the branch party of the locality; for instance,
the kuomintang groups in Provincial Assemblies
should be placed under the control of their
respective Provincial Executive Committees, the
Kuomintang groups in Parliament under the orders
of the Central Executive Committee and the Kuomintang
groups in labour organizations, clubs etc under the
control of the Executive Committee of the branches
in the locality.
Art. 62. Should members of a group be in disagreement a
meeting should be held by the Executive Committee
in charge of the group to discuss and settle the
matter. Should the Executive Committee be unable
to do so, it should then be submitted to the
higher Executive Committee.
Art. 63. With the permission of the Kuomintang group,
any member of the group may □□□□□□□□□□ join
any organizations. When a member of the Kuomintang
group in Parliament is appointed to take office
in the cabinet approval must first be obtained
from the group concerned and from the Central
Executive Committee.
Art. 64. All Kuomintang groups must elect their own
officers & organize a general business board for
the carrying out of the affairs of the group.
Art. 65. Kuomintangs who are members of any organization,
should hold an advance discussion of all problems
coming before that organization and to fix their
attitude in regard to these problems. Kuomintangs,
who are members of any organization, must act in
harmony. Different opinions may be expressed
at the meetings of the group, but at public meetings
the opinions of all Kuomintangs must harmonise.
A member violating this decision violates the
decisions of the Party and will be dealt with.
Art. 66. A member of the Party who is connected with any
Assembly must send in a letter of resignation from
that Assembly to the Executive Committee of the
branch party to which the group is attached to be
kept on file. In the event of his violating the
discipline of the Party the letter of resignation
will be taken out and published in the paper of the
Party; he will be required to sever his connection
with the Assembly with which he is attached.

第六十一条。国民党小组应服从当地党部执行委员会的命令；例如，省议会中的国民党小组应受各自省执行委员会的管辖，国会中的国民党小组应服从中央执行委员会的命令，劳工组织、俱乐部等中的国民党小组应受当地支部执行委员会的管辖。

第六十二条。若小组成员发生分歧，应由负责该小组的执行委员会召开会议讨论并解决此事。若执行委员会无法解决，则应提交上级执行委员会处理。

第六十三条。经国民党小组许可，任何小组成员均可□□□□□□□□□□加入任何组织。当国会中国民党小组的成员被任命入阁任职时，必须事先获得相关小组及中央执行委员会的批准。

第六十四条。所有国民党小组必须选举自己的职员，并组织总事务委员会以处理小组事务。

第六十五条。身为任何组织成员的国民党员，应对提交该组织审议的所有问题进行预先讨论，并确定其对这些问题的立场。身为任何组织成员的国民党员，行动必须保持一致。不同意见可在小组会议上表达，但在公开会议上，所有国民党员的意见必须保持一致。违反此决定的成员即违反党的决定，将受到处置。

第六十六条。与任何议会有关联的党员，必须向该小组所属的支部党部执行委员会提交辞去该议会职务的辞呈，以备存档。若其违反党纪，该辞呈将被取出并在党报上刊登；其将被要求切断与其所属议会的联系。
